text: Selective Knowledge Erasure in Large Language Models

This project proposes Adaptive Targeted Unlearning (ATU), a controller-based approach for selectively removing unwanted knowledge from Large Language Models (LLMs) while preserving useful retained knowledge. Traditional unlearning methods often rely on fixed training steps or constant optimization pressure, which can lead to over-erasure, degradation of retained knowledge, or incomplete removal of stubborn information. ATU addresses these limitations by continuously monitoring the model’s forgetting state and retained-knowledge performance, allowing the unlearning process to adapt its behavior based on the model’s current condition. The approach also uses development-time probing to identify information that remains recoverable and guide targeted unlearning. To evaluate the effectiveness of the approach beyond standard direct queries, an Automated Privacy Red-Team is used to test whether forgotten information can still be recovered through paraphrased, indirect, partial, completion-based, and follow-up queries. This provides a systematic framework for adaptive knowledge removal, retained-knowledge preservation, and evaluation of residual information recovery after unlearning.
Consider an LLM trained on information about multiple fictitious authors, including their biographies and specific facts.
Suppose information about one particular author must be removed, while information about all other authors should remain available.
A conventional unlearning method may apply the same forgetting pressure for a fixed number of steps.
Insufficient unlearning: the target information may still be recovered using indirect or adversarial queries.
Excessive unlearning: unnecessary optimization can damage useful retained knowledge.
Therefore, the system needs to determine how much unlearning is actually required, identify stubborn information, and stop before retained knowledge is unnecessarily affected.
Develop an adaptive machine-unlearning framework for LLMs.
Detect stubborn or recoverable target information.
Evaluate residual information recovery after unlearning.
• Machine Unlearning: Removes specific unwanted knowledge from a trained LLM while preserving other useful knowledge.
• Targeted Unlearning: Focuses forgetting on selected data or knowledge without retraining the entire model.
• LLM Unlearning: Applies unlearning techniques such as Gradient Ascent, NPO and representation-based methods to remove target information.
• Adaptive Unlearning: Dynamically adjusts the unlearning process based on the model’s current forgetting and retention state.
• Forget–Retain Trade-off: Ensures target information is suppressed while minimizing damage to retained knowledge.
• Leakage Detection: Uses development-time probes to identify target information that remains recoverable after unlearning.
• Adaptive Stopping: Stops unlearning when sufficient forgetting is achieved or when retained-knowledge performance starts degrading.
• Privacy Red-Team: Tests the final model using paraphrased, indirect, partial and adversarial queries to detect residual information recovery.
• Multi-Metric Evaluation: Evaluates forgetting, retention, model stability and residual recovery rather than relying on a single metric.
• Research Direction: Existing approaches mainly focus on unlearning effectiveness; ATU combines adaptive control, leakage detection, retention protection and automated recovery testing.
Title Name : Robust Privacy Unlearning for LLM Services via Adversarially Augmented Preference Optimization
Authors : Shuhan Yang, Yao Guan, Qiang Duan, Chenchi Luo, Haijun Yang.
Journal / conference : 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS), pp. 1210–1212. Work-in-progress conference paper.

Summary : This paper introduces Adversarially Augmented Preference Optimization (A²PO) for privacy unlearning in LLM services. It expands forget queries into adversarial variations, including paraphrases, contextual hints, prompt wrappers, and multilingual reformulations. The model is trained to prefer privacy-preserving substitute answers over sensitive disclosures. Experiments use the TOFU benchmark with Llama-2-7B and Llama-3.1-8B to evaluate forgetting under clean and adversarial queries.

Relevance : This closely matches your use of TOFU, preference-based unlearning, and adversarial leakage probes. It provides a comparison method for investigating whether ATU suppresses sensitive facts across different ways of asking a question. Its short work-in-progress format should be considered when assessing the depth of its evidence.
Title Name : Proof of Unlearning for Semantic Knowledge Bases in Large Language Models-Enabled Semantic Communication
Authors : Yijing Lin, Ze Chai, Jiacheng Wang, Zhipeng Gao, Nan Ma, Ping Zhang, Dusit Niyato.
Journal / conference : IEEE Communications Magazine, Volume 64, Issue 4, pp. 58–64.

Summary : The paper studies verifiable knowledge removal from LLM-enabled semantic knowledge bases. It proposes a model-agnostic proof-of-unlearning framework that tracks changes in the LoRA adapter subspace during unlearning. Successive reverse steps produce a proof trace that a verifier can examine to assess the unlearning process. The framework is evaluated experimentally in the context of semantic communication.

Relevance : Your project also modifies an LLM through LoRA adapters. This paper provides ideas for recording adapter changes and making the unlearning process auditable. Its application setting differs from TOFU, so its verification approach would need to be evaluated on your factual-erasure task.
Title Name : When Machine Unlearning Meets Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Keep Secret or Forget Knowledge?
Authors : Shang Wang, Tianqing Zhu, Dayong Ye, Wanlei Zhou.
Year : 2026 journal issue; first published online by IEEE in 2025.
Journal / conference : IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing, Volume 23, Issue 2, pp. 2030–2045.

Summary : This paper proposes a lightweight behavioral-unlearning framework using retrieval-augmented generation. It modifies an external knowledge base to influence the model’s responses without changing the target LLM’s parameters. The authors formulate the construction of unlearning knowledge as a constrained optimization problem and evaluate the approach on open-source and closed-source LLMs. The method aims to suppress sensitive disclosures while preserving general usefulness.

Relevance : This offers an alternative comparison for your parameter-based ATU method. It helps distinguish suppressing disclosure through retrieval and prompting from changing knowledge stored in model parameters. Your adversarial probes could help assess how these approaches differ in robustness.
Title Name : Learning to Unlearn While Retaining: Combating Gradient Conflicts in Machine Unlearning
Journal / conference : 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), pp. 4211–4221.

Summary : This paper examines conflicts between the gradients used to forget selected data and those used to preserve retained knowledge. Such conflicts can hinder optimization and reduce model utility. The proposed Learning to Unlearn while Retaining framework introduces an implicit gradient-regularization mechanism to reduce this interference. Experiments cover discriminative and generative tasks, assessing both forgetting effectiveness and performance on retained data.

Relevance : Your ATU objective combines a forgetting loss with a retention loss. This paper provides a useful explanation for why these objectives can interfere and suggests ways to improve update directions. Its ideas could inform your adaptive controller and retain-utility guard, with further testing required for Qwen and TOFU.
Title Name : Revisiting Machine Unlearning with Dimensional Alignment
Authors : Seonguk Seo, Dongwan Kim, Bohyung Han.
Journal / conference : 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV), pp. 3206–3215.

Summary : The authors analyze how unlearning affects latent feature representations. They introduce dimensional alignment, a metric that measures alignment between the eigenspaces of forget-set and retain-set representations. This metric is incorporated into an unlearning objective alongside self-distillation and alternating training. The paper also examines weaknesses in existing evaluation metrics and proposes tools for assessing forgetting and knowledge preservation more faithfully.

Relevance : Your project includes representation-based unlearning and aims to avoid damaging unrelated knowledge. This paper suggests representation-level diagnostics that could complement ROUGE, answer likelihood, and Truth Ratio. Applying its metric to LLM hidden states would require adaptation and validation.
Title Name : ULTRA: A Standardized Certification Metric for Machine Unlearning
Journal / conference : IEEE Access, Volume 14, pp. 66955–66970.

Summary : ULTRA introduces an evaluation framework covering behavioral similarity to retraining, membership indistinguishability, representation leakage, retained utility, robustness to post-unlearning interventions, and computational efficiency. It aggregates violations using a worst-case rule to prevent strong average results from concealing serious failures. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 identify persistent representation leakage and show that average-based evaluation can overestimate unlearning quality.

Relevance : This supports your decision to evaluate ATU beyond a single forgetting score. It suggests extending your leakage tests with internal-representation probes, membership-inference checks, and recovery tests after further adaptation. Its published experiments use image classifiers, so LLM-specific tests would be needed.
Title Name : Unrolling SGD: Understanding Factors Influencing Machine Unlearning
Authors : Anvith Thudi, Gabriel Deza, Varun Chandrasekaran, Nicolas Papernot.
Journal / conference : 2022 IEEE 7th European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P), pp. 303–319.

Summary : The paper investigates approximate unlearning by analyzing stochastic gradient descent. It studies verification error, measured through the difference between approximately unlearned model weights and weights obtained by retraining without the deleted data. The analysis produces an efficiently computable proxy for unlearning error and motivates a training penalty that limits overall weight changes. Experiments cover CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and IMDB sentiment analysis.

Relevance : This provides theoretical background for examining how optimization choices affect unlearning quality. It is useful when discussing ATU’s controlled updates and stopping behavior. It also clarifies why reduced target-answer likelihood alone does not establish equivalence to a model trained without the forgotten data.
Title Name : Auditing Approximate Machine Unlearning for Differentially Private Models
Authors : Yuechun Gu, Jiajie He, Keke Chen.
Year : 2025 conference publication; added to IEEE Xplore in 2026.
Journal / conference : 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), pp. 1253–1262.

Summary : This paper audits privacy risks for both forgotten and retained samples after approximate unlearning. It defines privacy criteria using differential privacy and membership-inference attacks, and introduces A-LiRA, an attack that uses data augmentation to reduce shadow-model training costs. The experiments show that approximate unlearning can increase privacy risks for retained samples even when the original model was trained with differential privacy.

Relevance : Your retain-utility guard checks whether useful knowledge survives unlearning. This paper suggests adding privacy checks for retained data as another evaluation dimension. Its central setting involves differentially private models; your current model would require a suitably adapted auditing protocol.
Title Name : Fast Yet Effective Machine Unlearning
Authors : Ayush K. Tarun, Vikram S. Chundawat, Murari Mandal, Mohan Kankanhalli.
Journal / conference : IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, Volume 35, Issue 9, pp. 13046–13055.

Summary : The paper proposes class-level unlearning using error-maximizing noise and an impair–repair procedure. The impairment stage uses generated noise to disrupt knowledge associated with targeted classes. The repair stage then restores performance using retained data. The method is evaluated on vision tasks and supports forgetting multiple classes with relatively few model-update steps.

Relevance : The impair–repair approach provides a useful comparison for balancing forgetting pressure and utility preservation. It can inform your discussion of damage caused by aggressive updates and the role of retention training. Its experiments concern class removal in vision models, making its connection to factual LLM erasure methodological.
Title Name : Boundary Unlearning: Rapid Forgetting of Deep Networks via Shifting the Decision Boundary
Authors : Min Chen, Weizhuo Gao, Gaoyang Liu, Kai Peng, Chen Wang.
Journal / conference : 2023 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 7766–7775.

Summary : Boundary Unlearning removes an entire class from a trained deep neural network by changing its decision boundary to approximate the behavior of a retrained model. The paper introduces two strategies, Boundary Shrink and Boundary Expanding. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and VGGFace2 evaluate class forgetting, retained performance, and privacy, reporting substantial reductions in unlearning time compared with full retraining.

Relevance : This provides background for targeted removal and the trade-off between forgetting, retained utility, and computational cost. Its retraining-based comparison is useful when designing evaluation references for ATU. The method addresses classification boundaries, so applying its principles to LLM factual knowledge would require a different implementation.

The system shall identify information that is exposed or recoverable from the model.
The system shall allow the user to select specific exposed information to be unlearned.
The system shall selectively unlearn the chosen information using the ATU controller.
The system shall monitor and preserve unrelated knowledge during the unlearning process.
The system shall test whether forgotten information can still be recovered using multiple attack and reformulated prompts.
The system shall compare the Target Model and Unlearned Model and generate a final evaluation report.
The system shall decide whether to continue, increase, reduce, or stop unlearning based on target state, leakage feedback, and retain performance.

6:      FOR EACH example x_i IN D_f DO:
9:              state[i] ← SUPPRESSED,  w_i(t) ← 0.0   // Decay: zero pressure on unlearned facts
10:         ELSE IF log_p ≥ τ_stubborn OR ProbeLeaks(x_i) THEN:
11:             state[i] ← STUBBORN,   w_i(t) ← 1.4   // Boost: amplify pressure on resistant facts
13:             state[i] ← UNLEARNING, w_i(t) ← 1.0   // Standard unlearning pressure
18:         BREAK  // Safety halt: Prevents collateral damage to unrelated knowledge
20:     IF ALL targets IN D_f ARE SUPPRESSED THEN:
21:         BREAK  // Early stopping: Target knowledge fully eliminated
24:     FOR EACH (batch_f, batch_r) IN DataLoader(D_f, D_r) DO:
25:         L_forget = ( Σ_i w_i(t) · L_NPO(θ, batch_f[i]) ) / Σ_i w_i(t)
29: RETURN θ  // Output safety-aligned unlearned model
